plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pink. It thrives in cold winter conditions and is prized for flowering when little else does in the garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to late winter (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Despite its name, the Christmas Rose is not a rose but belongs to the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: A bulbous perennial producing tall, sturdy stalks topped with large trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, garden plants bloom outdoors in summer, while in the north they are forced indoors for winter display.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to February); forced indoors in the Northern Hemisphere in winter
plants.location: Native to tropical and subtropical South America; cultivated worldwide, with outdoor blooming in Australia, South Africa, and South America
plants.funFact: A single large amaryllis bulb can produce several flower stalks, and the flower stalk can grow several centimeters in a single day.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with feathery fern-like leaves that becomes covered in brilliant clusters of flowers. Its blooms light up streets and parks in the warm season, followed by long woody seed pods.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to February), with some blooming in tropical regions at other times
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including northern Australia, Brazil, and parts of Africa
plants.funFact: In the wild in Madagascar it is endangered, even though it is among the most widely planted ornamental trees in the tropics.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and showy rose-like flowers. Many cultivars begin blooming in early winter, brightening gardens in mild-winter climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (December to April)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, Pacific Northwest, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil.
